stem: Which set lists the four teachable-learnable skills in the AHRQ TeamSTEPPS framework?

options.A: Communication, team leadership, situation monitoring, and mutual support
options.B: Communication, root-cause analysis, medication reconciliation, and mutual support
options.C: Team leadership, utilization review, delegation, and quality improvement
options.D: Situation monitoring, discharge planning, credentialing, and conflict reporting

rationale: AHRQ TeamSTEPPS 3.0 explicitly identifies four teachable-learnable teamwork skills: communication, team leadership, situation monitoring, and mutual support. Therefore A is correct. The other options mix genuine healthcare activities with terms that are not the four TeamSTEPPS core skills.
educational_objective: Recall the four TeamSTEPPS teamwork skills: communication, team leadership, situation monitoring, and mutual support.
source_organization: Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality (AHRQ)
source_document_title: TeamSTEPPS 3.0 — Section 1: Overview of Key Concepts and Tools
source_version_date: Page last reviewed July 2023; current TeamSTEPPS 3.0 curriculum rechecked 2026-08-17
source_locator: Key Concepts > Team Competency Outcomes; Key Skills for Effective Teamwork — four skills listed as Communication, Team Leadership, Situation Monitoring, and Mutual Support
source_claim_supported: TeamSTEPPS requires appropriate team structure and four teachable-learnable skills: Communication, Team Leadership, Situation Monitoring, and Mutual Support.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Management of Care, printed p.7/PDF p.11: Collaborate with members of the interprofessional health care team to facilitate client care; Participate in client care coordination
blueprint_topic: Management of Care — interprofessional teamwork competencies
correction_summary: Retained the correct TeamSTEPPS four-skill construct, moved the keyed answer from C to A, replaced obviously unrelated/negative distractor sets with more plausible healthcare-term combinations, and reduced difficulty from hard to easy because the final item is direct framework recall.

audit_findings.source_authority: PASS — AHRQ TeamSTEPPS 3.0 is the official federal framework directly defining the tested skills.
audit_findings.currentness: PASS — live TeamSTEPPS 3.0 overview rechecked 2026-08-17; no superseding TeamSTEPPS version identified.
audit_findings.exact_locator: PASS — Key Concepts and Key Skills for Effective Teamwork explicitly list all four keyed skills.
audit_findings.stem: PASS — directly asks for the framework's defined skill set without hidden application assumptions.
audit_findings.correct_answer: PASS — A exactly reproduces the four AHRQ-defined skills.
audit_findings.option_A: Correct — all four terms are explicitly listed by AHRQ.
audit_findings.option_B: Wrong but plausible — communication and mutual support are core skills, but root-cause analysis and medication reconciliation are not members of the four-skill set.
audit_findings.option_C: Wrong but plausible — team leadership is core, but utilization review, delegation, and quality improvement are not the remaining three TeamSTEPPS skills.
audit_findings.option_D: Wrong but plausible — situation monitoring is core, but discharge planning, credentialing, and conflict reporting are not the remaining skills.
audit_findings.rationale: PASS — makes only the exact framework claim and avoids unsupported outcome exaggeration.
audit_findings.educational_objective: PASS — specific to the four TeamSTEPPS skills.
audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: PASS — only A contains all four and no non-framework additions.
audit_findings.cueing: PASS — each option contains four healthcare/team-related terms in parallel form and comparable length.
audit_findings.blueprint: PASS — interprofessional collaboration and care coordination fit Management of Care.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: PASS — rechecked the live AHRQ page lines listing the four skills, currentness, NCSBN mapping, stem, all option sets, rationale, objective, ambiguity and cueing from zero.
